candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Exodus
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Exodus XXXII.4 (NPNF S2 V13, Gwynn/Schaff trans., Oxford 1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Exodus (c. 360 AD)

Moses' intercession after the golden calf, in which he pleads against the wrath of God on behalf of the people, is for Ephrem the canonical OT prefiguration of Christ's high-priestly intercession (Jn 17; Heb 7:25). The mediator does not stand with the accuser but with the accused, even when the accused are guilty. Tewahedo reads Ex 32:11 as the principal OT figure of mediatorial prayer.
candidates.reviewer_notes: Curated PD interpretive summary representing the Ethiopian Tewahedo tradition's reading via Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Exodus. Verify the summary still reflects the source's argument before promoting; substitute a verbatim quote from the NPNF / Charles dump where available, and where applicable cross-check the Andəmta homiletic tradition for resonance.

candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Exodus
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Exodus XXXII.10 (NPNF S2 V13, Gwynn/Schaff trans., Oxford 1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Exodus (c. 360 AD)

Moses breaks the first tablets at the foot of the mountain when he sees the calf; the second tablets are given after intercession and re-ascent. Ephrem reads the two givings as the canonical figure of the two Testaments: the first Adamic covenant broken at the foot of the mountain, the second covenant given through the One who ascends and descends. Tewahedo carries this as the principal OT figure of the OT-NT twofold canonical witness.

Ephrem reads the two givings as the canonical figure of the two Testaments: the first Adamic covenant broken at the foot of the mountain, the second covenant given through the One who ascends and descends. Tewahedo carries this as the principal OT figure of the OT-NT twofold canonical witness.
